beforeC2.minimalFixDirection: Evaluate the pre-handshake absolute deadline on every serve-loop iteration before accepting the next inbox item, independent of queue emptiness. Preserve original deadline (do not renew per rejected request), pre-handshake safe replies before the cutoff, normal negotiated sessions and controlled cleanup.
beforeC2.testDirection: Keep the actual default-duration counterexample as evidence; use a separately labeled short-limit deterministic busy-inbox regression if desired, without treating it as default-duration proof. Verify late hello is rejected/transport closes while idle deadline and normal timely hello still work.
beforeC2.limits: Demonstrates an approximately 0.73 s-or-greater actual default-budget overrun and late successful negotiation; does not claim an infinite lifetime or a performance/resource-exhaustion measurement.

sourceAndTestReview: The original absolute deadline is established once; every serve iteration checks session is None and monotonic >= deadline before reading the inbox. Busy and empty inbox paths now share the same cutoff; rejected requests cannot renew it.
A timely successful hello sets the negotiated session, so only the pre-handshake check is disabled. Normal negotiated request handling and original stop/Store/signal/temp cleanup remain unchanged.

Three new tests run actual serve/JSONL/contract/SQLite with module-local clock/stdin references replaced, without changing global modules or production LIMITS. Boundary exactly 5.0 and 6.0 reject late hello; timely hello followed by a repeated hello after cutoff still produces INVALID_STATE rather than killing the established session.
Actual default-time probes below complement the controlled-clock tests; the test itself is not called a default-duration experiment.
